title: Merged optimization targets
description: Output of the merge phase: deduplicated optimization targets ready for the optimizer fan-out. One target per unique structural change, possibly aggregating evidence from multiple family analyses. Convergence across analyses is high-confidence signal that the target is real.

merge_method.description: Identifier of which merge implementation produced this output. Reserved for future expansion if alternative merge implementations are added; currently only `llm` exists.

merge_model.description: The exact model identifier used for the merge call (e.g. 'gpt-5.3-codex-spark', 'gpt-5.3-codex'). Empty string only for the no-op empty-input case.

rejected_by_merge.description: Accepted analyses the merger affirmatively dropped (rare; e.g., recognized as already-shipped, scope-out reasons). Every accepted family_id from this session must appear in EXACTLY ONE of: a target's `merged_from`, OR this list.

id.description: Canonical kebab-case identifier; equal to the canonical fix_signature of this target group. Used as a path segment (experiments/<id>/) by Phase 2 onward.

merged_from.description: family_ids of the accepted analyses that contributed to this target.

convergence_count.description: Length of `merged_from`. Higher = independent analyses agreed on this fix = higher confidence.

rank.description: Optional priority ordering hint for the optimizer fan-out.

total_wall_us.description: Inclusive wall time of the target span. Required for parity with analysis.schema.json's hotspot requirement; the merge phase carries this through from the contributing analyses.

evidence.description: Canonical synthesis. When merging multiple analyses, the merger should preserve the strongest evidence from each contributor.

proposed_change.description: Canonical version of the change. When contributors phrased the change differently, the merger picks the most concrete and actionable wording.

merge_notes.description: Optional reviewer-facing note from the merger: why these analyses were collapsed, what was preserved, what was canonicalized.

contributor_differences.description: Optional: short bullets describing where contributors disagreed (different files cited, slightly different fix wording, divergent expected_improvement_pct). Useful for reviewers spot-checking the merge quality.
